text:
mike: UA: small pods pending in us-central1 even though node GPU utilization is low. scheduler keeps attempting to prebind to `nvlink-island=true` nodes then attach times out. provisioning keeps scaling spots and cost is rising.

hema: Any recent affinity/taint changes?

mike: Not on our side. Found several nodes with `nvlink-island=true` that were labelled during a capacity experiment. They now sit nearly empty (util < 5%) but marked NoSchedule. scheduler appears to still consider them as placement targets because of a legacy soft affinity plugin -> prebind race.

oliver: paste pod events?

mike: abridged: 
```
Events:
  Type    Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----    ------            ----  ----               -------
  Normal  Scheduled         4m    default-scheduler  Assigned default/train-small to node-usc1-45
  Warning FailedAttach      4m    attach-detach      AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pvc-1": rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded
  Warning FailedScheduling 2m    default-scheduler  Pod failed to fit: 0/60 nodes had available gpu, node(s) had taint: nvlink-island=true:NoSchedule
```

hema: That exact pattern caused yesterday's spot thrash. Quick wins: 1) hotpatch scheduler to run taint filter before prebind plugin 2) short-term flip orphaned island nodes to PreferNoSchedule 3) controller that adds age metadata and auto-relaxes stale taints.

sylvie: 1 is least invasive. 2 touches node state (risk to big-gang locality). 3 is better long-term. We should run 1 as a canary in usc1-b.

mike: Proposed canary plan: patch scheduler-config cm in kube-system on usc1-b to reorder plugins: evaluate taints early. Rolling window 15m, monitor `kube_scheduler_failed_scheduling`, `kube_scheduler_pre_binding_failures`, and spot node launch rate. Alert if spot launches > baseline*2 in 10m.

oliver: +1. I'll prepare the patch. Dry-run:
```
kubectl -n kube-system patch cm scheduler-config --patch '{"data": {"pluginOrder": "taint-filter,predicates,prebind"}}' --dry-run=client -o yaml
```
Posting PR to infra repo and tagging @hema @mike for review.

ops-bot: alert created: ALRT-5099 - usc1 spot provisioning surge. runbook: /runbooks/spot_scale_surges.md :warning:

hema: Also schedule a short audit to list `nvlink-island=true` nodes with util <10% and last heartbeat >6h; owners should confirm. If unowned, controller TTL can flip to PreferNoSchedule after 12h.

mike: Canary applied to usc1-b. Pending fell from 26 -> 5 in ~9m, spot launches reduced. Leaving canary for 30m then plan roll. If regression, fallback = mark orphaned islands PreferNoSchedule and notify owners.

sylvie: Please log cost delta. preliminary +$1.8k for the 4h window. Create follow-up ticket for controller RFC and add owner rotation for island nodes. Thanks all.
